item.title: Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist Dr Nanise Sikiti to share her story on fijivillage Her-Story
item.description: From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination. Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono on Wednesday at 7pm.
item.content:encoded:
From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination.

Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono on Wednesday at 7pm.

Dr Sikiti will share the beginning of her journey in humble surroundings in Levuka.

She will also speak about the sacrifices she has made throughout her career, the challenges of balancing family and professional responsibilities, and the people and experiences that have shaped the woman and doctor she is today.

You can watch fijivillage Her-Story on our facebook page, YouTube channel, and TikTok and X account, fijivillage at 7pm on Wednesday.

You can also catch the podcast, fijivillage Her-Story on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

item.title: Passport enrolment services suspended amid Immigration system upgrade
item.description: Passport enrolment services have been suspended from yesterday, until further notice due to an ongoing system upgrade. The Ministry of Immigration says members of the public should await further updates, with services expected to resume once the system has been fully restored.
item.content:encoded:
Passport enrolment services have been suspended from yesterday, until further notice due to an ongoing system upgrade.

The Ministry of Immigration says members of the public should await further updates, with services expected to resume once the system has been fully restored.

They say the disruption has led to frustration among members of the public who have turned up at the Immigration office seeking services.

A concerned member of the public told fijivillage News that people were turned away from the office and instead given a number to call before visiting.

She says staff were unable to provide a timeframe for when the system would be restored.

The woman also expressed frustration over what she described as a lack of timely communication about the disruption.

She claims there has been no update on the Immigration Department’s website since June 30th.

The Ministry further updates will be shared once services are fully restored.

Further questions have been sent to the Ministry of Immigration.

item.title: Fiji Labour Party opposes removal of $10,000 political donation limit
item.description: Fiji Labour Party is warning that removing the $10,000 limit on political donations could give wealthy and foreign interests greater influence over the country’s elections. The Party is strongly opposing proposed changes to electoral laws that would remove the existing cap on donations to political parties and individual candidates.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Labour Party is warning that removing the $10,000 limit on political donations could give wealthy and foreign interests greater influence over the country’s elections.

The Party is strongly opposing proposed changes to electoral laws that would remove the existing cap on donations to political parties and individual candidates.

Labour says the changes could increase the risk of undue influence, corruption and compromise electoral integrity.

The proposed amendments would also allow former Fiji citizens and non-citizens living overseas to make donations to political parties and candidates.

Labour says this is concerning, particularly as Fiji prepares for the next general election.

The proposed changes are currently before the Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights and are expected to come before Parliament when it resumes on 28th September.

Labour says the proposed changes, like the recent constitutional amendments, have been brought forward at the last minute, leaving limited time for proper public discussion and debate.

The party also acknowledges that the $10,000 donation limit had been abused by some political parties in the past, but says there was at least a level of control and accountability under the existing system.

Under the current system, political parties and candidates are required to disclose their election funding within 60 days after an election.

Labour says this means voters do not know before voting who may have financially influenced political parties or candidates.

The party also says the political playing field is already uneven ahead of the next general election.

Labour claims the three Coalition government parties — PAP, NFP and SODELPA — have received an annual grant of $325,000 since 2023 to meet expenses.

It says the grant was provided without public announcement or debate in Parliament and argues that this gives an advantage to the Coalition parties.

Labour says it has raised the issue with the Secretary-General to Parliament, the Electoral Commission and the Electoral Legislation Review Commission, but claims it has not received a response from the Secretary-General to Parliament or the Electoral Commission.

The party says removing the $10,000 donation cap could further increase the financial advantage of powerful political parties ahead of the next general election.

item.title: Nakasi resident raises concerns over alleged overnight liquor sales and disturbances
item.description: A Nakasi resident has raised concerns over alleged overnight liquor sales and disturbances linked to a shop on Ramesh Patel Street, off Vishnu Deo Road in Nakasi. The resident, who wishes to remain anonymous, claims the shop operates as a liquor outlet throughout the night, causing disturbances for people living nearby.
item.content:encoded:
A Nakasi resident has raised concerns over alleged overnight liquor sales and disturbances linked to a shop on Ramesh Patel Street, off Vishnu Deo Road in Nakasi.

The resident, who wishes to remain anonymous, claims the shop operates as a liquor outlet throughout the night, causing disturbances for people living nearby.

He alleges that private vehicles and taxis arrive at the shop throughout the night, with people gathering in the area to drink alcohol and play loud music.

The resident says intoxicated people sometimes fight in the area and bang on the fences of neighbouring properties.

He says concerns have been raised with the Nakasi Police Station, but claims no action has been taken to address the issue.

The resident is calling on the relevant authorities to urgently look into the matter, saying they want peace and quiet in their neighbourhood.

Meanwhile, Police have said that they will look into the issue.
